In this writ petition, the petitioner has sought for writ of mandamus against respondent No.3 to pass an award under Section 23 and 30 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short New Act 2013) as the land belonging to the petitioner has been utilized for the purpose of road formation by the Sri Chowdappa V vs The Chief Secretary on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22191330/

sentences.text: 2. The relevant facts for the adjudication of this writ petition are that, the petitioner had purchased the land bearing Sy.No.205 of Santhekallahalli Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk and District as per registered sale deed dated 13.03.2006.

It is the case of the petitioner that, the portion of the land belonging to the petitioner has been acquired by the respondent-authorities for the improvement of road from B.C. Road to K.G. Pura at NC: 2024:KHC:44989 Chintamani Taluk and therefore, it is the grievance of the petitioner that though the land belonging to the petitioner has been utilized for the purpose of formation of road, however, no compensation has been granted to the petitioner and therefore, the petitioner has approached the respondent authorities stating that, 8 guntas of the land belonging to the petitioner has been utilized for the purpose of road improvement work as per the circular dated 27.07.2001.

In that view of the matter, this Court vide order dated 06.04.2023 observes as follows:
"This Court vide order dated 27.03.2023 said as under:
The Executive Engineer, Chickballapura, is directed to be present before the Court to offer explanation as to why the compensation determined years ago has not been paid to the Petitioner especially when his land was appropriated for the public purpose without due acquisition process.
He should also show cause as to why reasonable interest payable from his own pocket along with heavy costs should not be levied.
If he does not appear pursuant to this order on the next date of hearing, he runs the risk of being arrested and brought before the Court.
Call this matter for Further Hearing on 06.04.2023.
A Copy of this order shall be shared with learned AGA.
The Registry is directed to send a copy of this order by Speed Post to the said address for compliance, right now.

Pursuant to the said order, Sri. B. Thimarayappa, Executive Engineer, Public Works Department,
Chickballapaura, is present before the Court and has filed an affidavit producing as many as five documents (R1 to R5).

A perusal of the Affidavit and the accompanying documents does not leave any doubt as to the private land of the Petitioner having been utilized for the formation of the road sans accomplishment of the acquisition process.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner is more than justified in submitting that Right to Property having been constitutionally guaranteed under Article 300A, touching private property sans acquisition process is a constitutional sin.
The sin having been perpetrated there should atonement of the same by the parties by paying the compensation/damages for the land taken.

sentences.text: Learned AGA submits that the determination of the so called damages (compensation sic) to the tune of Rs.59,17,803/- is on the higher side regard being had to the town in question and the location of the property concerned and therefore, NC: 2024:KHC:44989 there is some objection from the Government side.
He seeks a period of two weeks for ascertaining & accomplishing the true & correct valuation of the subject property, and to come out with fresh determination.

Reluctantly, a period of two weeks is granted subject to the condition that within the said period,
there should be determination of the compensation/damages and the Respondents should come with a Bank draft on the next date of hearing, failing which, the lapsing officials may run the risk of being arrested & brought before the Court.
Call this matter for Further Hearing on 20.04.2023."

3. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that respondent No.4 has already quantified the compensation of Rs.59,17,803/- as per Annexure-Q and the same has to be considered by respondent No.3 while passing the award insofar as the acquisition of the land belonging to the petitioner is concerned.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that, he has secured NC: 2024:KHC:44989 the relevant sale deeds in which the land in the same vicinity has been sold and also he has secured the compensation to be awarded in favour of the petitioner in respect of the land sold in the same vicinity and the copy of the same is produced at page No.16 of the list of documents produced before this Court.

Therefore, it is contended that while taking into consideration, the lands which have been sold in the same vicinity, approximately the petitioner in this matter would get more than Rs.53,00,000/- and therefore, it is contended that, there is no impediment for respondent No.3 to pass award taking into consideration the sale deeds referred to by the petitioner before this Court.
4.

In that view of the matter, considering the fact that the petitioner being a land looser is entitled for the compensation as required under Article 300A of the Constitution of India, I am of the view that, respondent No.3 is directed to pass the award in accordance with law taking into account the sale deeds said to have been NC: 2024:KHC:44989 produced by the petitioner herein to quantify the compensation to be arrived at insofar as the land belonging to the petitioner has been utilized for the purpose of formation of the road.
It is made clear that the petitioner herein is entitled for the compensation under the New Act of 2013 since no award has been passed yet by the respondent-authorities.
Taking into consideration the observations made above, respondent Nos.3 and 4 shall pass the award within two months from the date of receipt of this order.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.
